titre: Trois sujets déjà réglés : un seul a vraiment du neuf (#240 fait perdre des événements à Orbitly), les deux autres reviennent sans rien de nouveau

regles: PR #240 is merged and deployed: replayed batches are now deduplicated by event_id.
The 12/11 backfill is finished; Orbitly and Zest Grocers have complete data again.
Your root-cause section of the 12/11 postmortem is in issue #233.

source.titre: rachel in #support-escalations: Orbitly says their iOS funnel numbers dropped

tours.texte: rachel in #support-escalations: "Orbitly says their iOS funnel numbers dropped ~8% since last Friday, their PM asks if it's related to the incident". friday = when 240 went out. check if the dedupe drops real events. orbitly project_id = prj_0rb1

I'll compare what #240's dedupe dropped for `prj_0rb1` since it was deployed (2026-11-13 09:40 UTC) with the rest of the projects.

The dedupe in `internal/dedupe/dedupe.go` keys on `event_id` only, with a 72h window in Redis. Drops are logged at debug level, which is off in prod, so I'll use the Prometheus counter `ingest_dedupe_dropped_total` instead.

`ingest_dedupe_dropped_total{project="prj_0rb1"}` since 13/11 09:40: **1,184,302** drops. All other projects together: 9,870. Orbitly alone is 99% of the drops. A replay after a Kafka rebalance (the 12/11 case) would hit every project roughly in proportion to its volume, so this doesn't look like replays.
sample 20 dropped ones and the event they were deduped against

Sampled 20 dropped events from the landing bucket and the kept event with the same `event_id`:

```
event_id  kept (device, ts, name)            dropped (device, ts, name)
17        d-8f2c 13/11 09:14 screen_view     d-a91e 13/11 11:02 add_to_cart
17        d-8f2c 13/11 09:14 screen_view     d-03bd 14/11 18:40 checkout_start
4         d-55e0 15/11 07:01 app_open        d-c7a2 15/11 21:13 app_open…

Found the cause. Every dropped event carries `sdk: kestrel-ios/3.2.0`, and its `event_id` is a small integer. Our own iOS SDK 3.2.0 changelog says: "event_id is now a per-session sequence number (smaller payloads)". It used to be a UUID. Our ingest contract says event_id is globally unique, so #240's dedupe treats event 17 of one session as a duplicate of event 17 of any other session within 72h.
ugh. so it's our own sdk. key the dedupe on (project_id, device_id, event_id) then. is device_id always there?

`device_id` is required by the ingest schema since v2 (`schema/event.go:41`, validation rejects events without it), and the landing data agrees: 0 events without `device_id` across all projects since 01/11. I'll change `dedupe.Key()` to `project_id:device_id:event_id` and keep the 72h window.

Done. Changed `dedupe.Key()` and added tests:
- same `event_id`, different devices → both kept
- same `event_id`, same device, replayed batch → dropped (the 12/11 replay case is still covered by `TestDedupeDropsReplayedBatch`)
- key includes project, so two customers can't collide

`go test ./internal/dedupe/...` ok, `go test ./...` ok (412 tests), `golangci-lint run` clean.
how many real events did we actually lose for orbitly. exclude genuine replays

Re-ran the dedupe over the raw landing data for `prj_0rb1` from 13/11 09:40 to now, with the new key. Of the 1,184,302 drops, 1,179,950 would be kept by the new key and 4,352 are genuine replays. So about **1.18 million legitimate Orbitly events were dropped**, ≈8.1% of their iOS volume over the period — which matches the drop their PM sees in the funnels.
anyone else on ios 3.2?

Projects sending `kestrel-ios/3.2.0` since 13/11: `prj_0rb1` (Orbitly) and `prj_z3st` (Zest Grocers, which has 3.2.0 on a pilot store app only: 0.4% of their traffic). Zest lost 3,812 events the same way. Everyone else is on 3.1.x or Android. So Zest is marginally affected too.
ok. open the PR, maya reviews. and write a note for the ios team: the sdk has to go back to uuids for event_id, this will bite again

Opened PR #247 "dedupe: key on (project, device, event_id), stop dropping Orbitly iOS events" with @maya-cohen as reviewer. Draft note for the iOS team:

> kestrel-ios 3.2.0 sends `event_id` as a per-session counter. Ingest dedupes on it (with device since #247), but the contract says event_id is a UUID and other consumers rely on that. Please restore UUIDs in 3.2.1. Affected: Orbitly, Zest pilot…
the orbitly rebackfill: can we replay from landing for 13/11 onward once 247 is merged

Yes. Landing keeps 30 days, so 13/11 onward is still there. `go run ./cmd/replay --project prj_0rb1 --from 2026-11-13T09:40:00Z --to <deploy time of #247>` with the new key reinserts the ~1.18M events and skips the 4,352 genuine replays; about 40 minutes. It must run only **after #247 is deployed**, otherwise the old key drops them again. Same command for `prj_z3st`, a few seconds.
yep after deploy. remind me
Will do: once #247 is merged and deployed, run the replay for Orbitly (and Zest) from 13/11, then check that `ingest_dedupe_dropped_total{project="prj_0rb1"}` stays near zero.

source.titre: #247 dedupe: key on (project, device, event_id), stop dropping Orbitly iOS events

tours.texte: kestrel-ios 3.2.0 sends event_id as a per-session counter, so the event_id-only dedupe from #240 drops distinct events from different devices. This keys the dedupe on project_id:device_id:event_id. Replays of the same batch are still dropped (test kept). Orbitly events dropped since 13/11 need a replay from landing after this is deployed.
Logic looks right, I'll approve once CI is green. Before we merge: how many Orbitly events did we drop since #240? I want the number for Thursday's call with Orbitly. @lior-bd

Root cause section added: during the 12/11 Kafka rebalance the consumer group re-read ~40 minutes of batches, which were re-ingested without any dedupe. Fixed by #240 (dedupe by event_id). Backfill done for Orbitly and Zest.
Final version is up, thanks all. Lior's root cause section made this easy. I'll present it at Friday's incident review; action items are in the Fathom notes.
Bumps the Go toolchain in CI and the Dockerfile from 1.23.2 to 1.23.4. No code change.
LGTM, merged.

faits.texte: Says the event_id-only dedupe from #240 has been dropping legitimate Orbitly iOS events since 13/11.
Gives the cause: Kestrel's own iOS SDK 3.2.0 sends event_id as a per-session counter instead of a UUID.
Says his fix PR #247 (dedupe keyed on project, device and event_id) is open, waiting for Maya's approval.
Says Maya wants the number of dropped Orbitly events before Thursday's call with Orbitly.
Gives that number: about 1.18 million events (≈8% of Orbitly's iOS volume).
Says the Orbitly replay from landing (from 13/11) is still to run, only after #247 is deployed.
Says he has an action item: an alert when the ingest dead-letter queue exceeds 1,000 messages, before Friday's incident review (20/11).
Says Zest Grocers is marginally affected too (3,812 events, pilot app on SDK 3.2.0).
